findings.problem: QuoteWorkflow mixes status:String with lifecycle booleans (is_validated, is_sent) and optional timestamp, allowing inconsistent states like is_sent=true with status="pending" or is_sent=true with sent_at_epoch_ms=None
findings.failure_mode: Callers and mutations can place the workflow into logically impossible states that the type system cannot catch
findings.fix: Replace status:String + is_validated:bool + is_sent:bool + sent_at_epoch_ms:Option<u64> with a single QuoteStatus enum (e.g. Pending, Validated, Sent) and derive sent_at_epoch_ms from the Sent variant. Eliminate all public field mutations.

findings.problem: All fields are pub on QuoteWorkflow, allowing external code to mutate status, booleans, and timestamp without any invariant enforcement
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can directly assign item.is_sent = false after mark_sent() was called, bypassing all workflow invariants
findings.fix: Make all fields private, provide a sealed constructor, and expose only invariant-preserving transitions via methods or fallible constructors.

findings.problem: Three independent primitives (status: String, is_validated: bool, is_sent: bool) encode a lifecycle but have no ordering or mutual-exclusion constraints enforced by the type system
findings.failure_mode: Runtime logic must re-check inconsistent states; bugs slip through when code assumes e.g. is_sent implies status=="sent"
findings.fix: Model the lifecycle as an enum typestate: enum QuoteStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } } with transitions enforced at the type level.

findings.problem: Raw primitives (String, bool, Option) enter the domain struct directly without a parse boundary or smart constructor
findings.failure_mode: Callers can construct QuoteWorkflow with arbitrary strings, invalid boolean combinations, and inconsistent data without any validation
findings.fix: Parse at the boundary into newtypes and enum variants through fallible constructors (e.g. impl TryFrom<(String, String, bool, bool, Option<u64>)> for QuoteWorkflow or dedicated smart constructors per variant).

findings.problem: mark_sent blindly overwrites status to "sent" and sets is_sent=true without checking preconditions (e.g. was it validated first?). It also leaves sent_at_epoch_ms as None despite the name implying it should be set.
findings.failure_mode: A quote can be marked sent without ever being validated, and sent_at_epoch_ms remains None, so downstream code relying on the timestamp will encounter None unexpectedly
findings.fix: Return Result<QuoteWorkflow, QuoteError> that rejects the transition if not in Validated state, and populate sent_at_epoch_ms. Replace with a typed transition method or dedicated constructor.

findings.problem: mark_sent returns QuoteWorkflow directly instead of Result<QuoteWorkflow, E>, giving no way to encode failure when the transition is invalid (e.g. not validated)
findings.failure_mode: Invalid transitions cannot be reported to callers; the function either silently does the wrong thing or callers must inspect the result for inconsistencies
findings.fix: Return Result<QuoteWorkflow, QuoteTransitionError> and define a typed error enum covering InvalidState, AlreadySent, etc.

findings.problem: mark_sent takes ownership and mutates fields then returns - it is an imperative action, not a pure calculation. There is no separation between the pure domain model and the imperative transition logic.
findings.failure_mode: The transition logic cannot be unit-tested in isolation without constructing the full workflow struct with its inconsistent state
findings.fix: Define a pure transition function: fn try_mark_sent(QuoteWorkflow) -> Result<QuoteWorkflow, QuoteError> that validates preconditions and returns a new value, or model transitions as enum variants.

findings.problem: No benchmarks exist for QuoteWorkflow construction, transitions, or any stated performance characteristics
findings.failure_mode: Performance claims cannot be validated; allocation patterns of String/Option fields are unmeasured
findings.fix: Add cargo bench benchmarks for workflow construction and state transitions with measured baseline, workload description, and variance.

findings.problem: No allocation profiling, no use of smallvec/cow/caller-owned buffers for id: String, and no evidence that String allocation for id is justified
findings.failure_mode: If id is short-lived or small, heap allocation is unnecessary overhead; if id is passed through many layers, &str or Cow would reduce allocations
findings.fix: Profile allocation patterns; consider &str or Cow<str> for id if the lifetime allows, or document why owned String is required.

missing_evidence: no profiler output showing allocation patterns
no command evidence (cargo test / cargo clippy / cargo fmt) executed
no second-ring review or formal verification evidence
residual_risk: The crate has fundamental typestate and invariant violations that cannot be assessed without repair. The struct allows arbitrary invalid state combinations, mark_sent has no precondition checking, and no evidence gates are present. This crate would fail any Holzman Rust gate without the enum typestate restructuring.
